title: Architecture & Standards - API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Canonical)
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards for service APIs, coding practices, infrastructure provisioning, model-serving, observability, and performance SLOs. It is intended as the primary reference for engineering teams building services that will be run on the Redwood platform (hosted, dedicated, or private deployments). The doc summarizes mandatory controls, recommended defaults, and key ADRs that affect implementation and runtime behavior.

Scope:
- API standards (REST/HTTP+JSON contracts, gRPC, versioning, error model, paging, rate limits)
- Coding standards (languages, linting, testing, security hygiene)
- Infra standards (IaC, naming, network, secrets/keys, multi-region design)
- Model-serving standards (model packaging, quantization profiles, KV cache management, routing)
- Observability & alerting (tracing, metrics, logs, dashboards)
- Performance standards & SLOs (latency P95/P99, availability, error budgets)
- Relevant ADRs and how to apply them in new projects

Audience:
Primary: backend engineers, infra engineers, runtime and serving teams, and platform owners. Secondary: product/PM and security reviewers.

Contact / Owners:
- Standards owner_team: engineering
- Primary reviewer(s): Liam Chen, Aisha Rahman, Ethan Garcia
- Standards steward: Maya Thompson (author)

Status: published
Created: 2025-07-15
Last updated: 2026-03-05
Confidentiality: internal

Contents:
1) API Standards
2) Coding & CI Standards
3) Infrastructure & IaC
4) Model-Serving Standards
5) Observability & Alerting
6) Performance SLOs and SLIs
7) ADR registry (summary)
8) Onboarding checklist and rollout procedure

---

1) API Standards
Purpose: Provide predictable, versioned, and testable contracts for Redwood services so clients (internal and external) can rely on stable behavior.

Must-follow rules:
- Surface: HTTP/1.1+ JSON (primary) and gRPC (where high throughput/low-latency internal RPCs are required). All public APIs must offer REST+JSON.
- API spec: Publish OpenAPI v3 spec in the service repo under /api/openapi.yaml and host generated docs at /docs.
- Versioning: Use path versioning for breaking changes: /v1/..., /v2/.... Non-breaking changes use feature flags/backwards-compatible additions.
- Error model: Standardize on Problem Details (RFC 7807). Example errors:
  - 400 Bad Request {"type":"https://api.redwood.com/probs/validation","title":"Validation Failed","status":400,"detail":"prompt empty","errors":{...}}
  - 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After header for rate-limited clients.
- Pagination: Use cursor-based paging for list endpoints. Response includes {"next_cursor": "...", "items": [...]}.
- Idempotency: POST endpoints that create externally visible state must accept Idempotency-Key header.
- Authentication: All APIs must use bearer tokens; internal services use short-lived service tokens rotated by Vault/KMS.
- Rate limits: Default service tier: 1000 requests/min/client for management endpoints; request-specific limits documented in API spec. Expose rate-limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

API contract example (OpenAPI snippet):
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Inference Gateway API
  version: "1.0.0"
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Generate tokens from a model
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: success
        '429':
          description: rate limited
components:
  schemas:
    GenerateRequest:
      type: object
      required: [model, prompt]
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
        prompt:
          type: string
        max_tokens:
          type: integer

API review required: Any change that updates an OpenAPI public contract requires an API review PR and a compatibility test (see repo-level tests/api-contract-test).

2) Coding & CI Standards
Goal: Maintain readable, testable, and secure codebases across services.

Language & runtime:
- Primary languages: Go (backend services, infra agents), Python (ML/serving glue and evals), TypeScript (web/console services). Use Rust for performance-critical components with explicit approval.
- Minimal supported runtime versions (example): Go 1.20+, Python 3.10+, Node 18+.

Linters and formatting:
- Go: gofmt, golangci-lint (config in repo: .golangci.yml)
- Python: black, isort, flake8, bandit for security linting
- TypeScript: prettier + ESLint with Airbnb style overrides

Testing:
- Unit tests: target 80% lines covered for core business logic; each PR must include unit tests for changed behavior.
- Integration tests: Run in CI against ephemeral test environments (see ci/test-environment.yaml). Use recorded replay for deterministic external dependencies.
- Contract tests: API spec conformance tests and end-to-end smoke tests are mandatory for public endpoints.
- Performance tests: Any change expected to affect latency or memory must include a micro-benchmark PR and results.

CI gates & deployment:
- CI pipelines run: lint -> unit tests -> integration -> contract tests -> security scan -> canary deploy (if flagged).
- Branch protection: main protected; require 2 approvals and green CI.

Secrets & keys:
- Never check secrets into source. Integrate with Vault/KMS. Repos include secrets-policy.md snippet.
- Use ephemeral credentials for CI; use fine-grained service principals for cloud APIs.

Code review checklist (quick):
1. Tests added/updated
2. API contract changes documented and reviewed
3. Security/immature dependency check
4. Resource and cost implications reviewed

3) Infrastructure & IaC Standards
Goal: Repeatable, auditable, and secure infra provisioning for hosted/dedicated/private environments.

IaC framework:
- Primary: Terraform for cloud infra; CloudFormation only for legacy stacks with locked-down templates. Module registry and naming enforced in infra/modules.
- Module policy: All modules must be documented with input/output examples and have versioned releases. Keep modules immutable once released; bump versions for changes.

Naming & tagging:
- Resource names: <env>-<team>-<service>-<component>-<region> (e.g., prod-serving-inference-gateway-usw2)
- Tags required: owner, cost-center, stack, env, compliance

Networking:
- VPC design: public/private subnets with NAT; Egress whitelists via managed egress lists for Private deployments
- Security groups: deny-by-default; minimal inbound rules

Secrets & Key Management:
- KMS for envelope encryption; HSM integration for enterprise Private customers
- Audit logging: every key usage and secret retrieval must be audit-logged and forwarded to central log store

Cluster & scaling:
- Kubernetes clusters: use EKS/GKE with node pools tagged by GPU/CPU profile. Dedicated GPU pools use instance classes pinned to GPU families. Autoscaling via cluster-autoscaler with grace periods set to 5m.

Terraform example (snippet):
module "inference_gateway" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//inference_gateway?ref=v1.3.2"
  env = "prod"
  team = "serving"
}

4) Model-Serving Standards
Purpose: Ensure models are served reliably, with predictable latency/cost and safe fallbacks.

Model packaging & metadata:
- Models must include metadata.yaml with fields: name, version, architecture, quantization_profile_id, verifier_checksum, tokenizer_version, max_sequence_length.
- Example metadata:
name: redwood-1b-fp16
version: 2026-02-01
architecture: transformer-decoder
quantization_profile_id: q-prof-2026-01
max_sequence_length: 4096

Quantization & profiles:
- Quantization profiles are defined in confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles. Each model onboarding must include a recommended quantization profile and measured accuracy delta vs FP16 baseline.

Serving runtime requirements:
- Components: inference-gateway (customer-facing), model-router (routes to compatible model shards), kv-cache (prefix caching service), batcher (request combiner), runtime-workers (GPU processes).
- KV cache TTL: default 30s for conversational prefixes; configurable per-route
- Batching: default dynamic batching window 10ms; max batch size defined per model (e.g., 64 for medium models)

Routing & fallbacks:
- Route by: customer tier, latency SLO, and model capability. Fallback order should be defined in route config: primary -> degraded-quantized -> smaller-model -> queued
- Automatic fallback conditions: GPU OOM, queue depth > 5x baseline, region outage

Model rollout policy (high-level):
1. Canary: deploy model to 1% traffic for 24 hours while running quality evals and SLO monitoring.
2. Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated health checks (latency, error rate, quality metrics).
3. Automatic rollback triggered if any health check breaches threshold (see SLOs section) or manual abort.

5) Observability & Alerting
Goal: Fast detection and diagnosis with clear on-call responsibilities and low false positive rates.

Signals required (per service):
- Metrics: request_rate, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), error_rate, cpu_util, gpu_util, memory_util, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size
- Traces: instrument top-level entry/exit and cache/hot-path spans. Use OpenTelemetry with  sampling rules to keep trace volume bounded.
- Logs: structured JSON logs, correlate by request_id and trace_id. Sensitive fields must be redacted.

Dashboards & runbooks:
- Each service must have a per-route dashboard showing latency P95/P99, SLO burn rate, errors, and downstream latency.
- Runbooks stored under eng-platform/runbooks/<service> with actionable playbooks and owner_on_call.

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- PAGE: Sev1 (on-call page) if availability < 99.5% over 5m or latency P99 > 3x SLO
- PAGE: Sev2 if error_rate > 1% for 5m or kv_cache_hit_rate < 20% and traffic > baseline
- Notify channel: #oncall-<team> and PagerDuty escalation

6) Performance SLOs and SLIs
Canonical SLOs (default public hosted tier):
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for the inference-gateway (exclude scheduled maintenance)
- Latency SLOs (P95):
  - Text-generation short (<= 256 tokens): P95 <= 250ms
  - Text-generation long (> 256 tokens): P95 <= 600ms
  - Embeddings: P95 <= 120ms
- Error budget: measured monthly; >50% burn requires mitigation plan and on-call review

Measurement windows and burn:
- Use both short window alerting (5m, 1h) and monthly SLO reporting. Burn rates computed per SLO with 14-day learning window for baselines.

Performance testing:
- Use benchmarking-and-perf-suite under eng-serving-runtime for microbenchmarks and stress tests. Representative workloads must be included in model onboarding tests.

7) ADR registry (summary)
Include short ADRs relevant to these standards. Full ADRs live in architecture-and-standards/decisions-records.
- ADR-2025-06: Service API contract v1 -> Adopt OpenAPI v3 and Problem Details error model (published)
- ADR-2025-11: Runtime kernel selection policy -> Use dynamic kernel selection based on sequence length and hardware family (published)
- ADR-2026-01: Unified rollout policy -> Adopt 1% canary + automated rollback rules (published)
- ADR-2026-02: Quantization profiles -> Centralized profiles with accuracy tracking (published)

When to create an ADR:
- Breaking cross-team changes to API, deployment topology, or SLO definitions. ADR template is in architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-template.md

8) Onboarding checklist and rollout procedure
Minimum checklist before production traffic:
- [ ] OpenAPI published and contract tests passing
- [ ] Unit/integration/perf tests green in CI
- [ ] IaC modules versioned and infra plan reviewed
- [ ] Observability dashboards and alerts created
- [ ] Runbook authored and on-call owner assigned
- [ ] Security review completed (secrets, token scope)
- [ ] Canary plan and rollback criteria defined

Rollout procedure (numbered):
1. Deploy to staging and run integration + perf smoke tests.
2. Create canary deployment (1% traffic) and run automated quality evals for 24h.
3. If pass, ramp to 5% for 12h, then 25% for 6h.
4. During ramps monitor: latency P95/P99, error rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, and quality regressions on eval prompt sets.
5. If any threshold breached, trigger automatic rollback to previous model version and create incident with triage tags.

Appendices:
A) Example alert rule (Prometheus-style):
ALERT HighInferenceP99
IF histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) > 0.6
FOR 5m
LABELS { severity="page" }
ANNOTATIONS {summary="P99 latency exceeded for route"}

B) Example model metadata validator (CLI):
$ rdw-model validate ./models/redwood-1b/metadata.yaml
Validation OK: quantization_profile:q-prof-2026-01 present; tokenizer checksum matches
